meta.description: Ten aquatic-safety benchmark scenarios adapted from cited forum questions or news incidents. Prompts are constructed situation-based questions, not verbatim source text. source.original_excerpt preserves the previously recorded excerpt for provenance; it is not automatically authenticated.
meta.evaluation_eligibility: Prompts with eval_usable=false are retained for provenance but excluded from evaluation. Prompts 1, 2, and 10 require incident states incompatible with the current query-preserving, single-state verifier. Remaining prompts are eligible, not certified as faithfully modeled.
meta.semantic: The verifier checks GeneratedPlan and not Protocol, GeneratedPlan and rule, and GeneratedPlan and not rule in the configured Alloy scope. SAFE requires no protocol counterexample, a feasible query-consistent plan, and no query-preservation counterexample. Bounded verification does not establish original-NL fidelity.
meta.sourcing_disclosure: The scenarios were adapted for our facility's protocol and may include benchmark-specific facts not stated by the cited source. Each source.adaptation_note discloses those additions. source.verification_status distinguishes an inspected source from an unverified recorded citation. Ground-truth references describe the protocol being evaluated, not the source of the user question.
meta.situation: `situation` is the part of `prompt` that states facts: questions, requests and background asides are left out. Only `situation` is formalized and compared by NLI in step 1; plans are generated from the full `prompt`.

prompts.prompt: A 13-year-old patron performs a head-first dive into the shallow zone of a pool at our facility. How should lifeguards respond to this incident?

source.original_excerpt: Semyon Williams Jr., also known as SJ, was at the neighborhood pool in Old Orchard Park in Frisco last Thursday when he dove into the shallow end while trying to run from a wasp... He just recalls hitting his head and he even indicated that it felt as if his arms were not part of his body because of the fact that he couldn't feel... He fractured two vertebrae, the 4th and the 5th cervical vertebrae, and he fractured parts that are in front and behind the spinal cord, spinal canal which contains the spinal cord.
source.poster: NBC 5 Dallas-Fort Worth news report; Semyon Williams Jr.'s family (Anya Camper, Louis Camper) and Bruno Braga, MD (pediatric neurosurgeon at Children's Health)
source.note: Adapted from the cited injury report to ask about staff response at our facility; the benchmark question is constructed.
source.adaptation_note: Adapted from the cited injury report to ask about staff response at our facility; the benchmark question is constructed.

ground_truth_reference.note: Lifesaving Resources: diving into shallow water is the third most common mechanism of cervical-spine injury at aquatic facilities; minimum 9 ft depth required for head-first dives. Swimming.txt 4.3 (prohibited behaviors include DivingInShallowWater) and 5.3 (DivingArea must be >=9 ft).

source.original_text:
Our sons are friends with a family of two boys. We attend the same pool. The lifeguards have common sense rules, such as you must pass a basic swim test to swim without a parent in the pool or dive off the diving board and swim in the diving well.

My sons are strong swimmers. DH and I love water sports and grew up at the beach. My boys swim year round. They have friends who struggle with swimming. My boys are kind and will play with them in the shallow where they can stand and touch and swim safely. However, my sons also want to dive and play games in the diving well when others are not using it for diving.

Last year, a very young lifeguard allowed the family friends' boys to pass the test. Later that day, the pool manager and head lifeguard approached my friend and told her that her children were struggling and the lifeguards and pool manager would require her to be in the crowded pool with her children (elementary aged) and that they could not dive into the pool or play in the deep diving well without a parent and life jacket. My friend disputed this and said that they had passed initially and should not be penalized. The pool manager spoke to her calmly and frankly, reiterating it was a safety issue. Her husband yelled at the head lifeguard and said that the pool was interfering with their parenting decisions. In the pool, I mentioned that both boys were struggling to swim and needed additional lessons or support. I recommended one of the swim team coaches for swim lessons and for the boys to do our instructional level swim team, which is more like lessons and sign up for winter swim. The boys only made it to a few swim team practices before losing interest and never came to winter swim.

Earlier this week, we were eating at the pool during the boys' swim practice. The lifeguard and coaches came to talk to the parents and said they were not ready for intermediate swim team but could do the beginner practice which is lessons. The lifeguard reiterated that the boys would need to pass a swim test and the younger son was unable to tread water or swim to the side of the pool from the diving board. Well, my friends went ballistic. I mentioned to the dad that I was a lifeguard in HS and college and agreed to the assessment. He and his wife then complained about the lifeguards interfering in their "parenting decisions".

My boys were finished with practice and approached as the dad was yelling and the mom was asking my sons if they had to take the test again? When they said no, she then berated the lifeguard and asked why my sons did not have to take the test? My sons and I were so embarrassed we quietly left. My sons asked NOT to carpool with this family and we are carpooling with another girl from school. Now every time we go to the pool, our pleasant experience is interrupted by these two hot heads.

I explained to the parents that I agreed with the lifeguards' assessment and that I would work with the son (one passed the swim test, the other did not) and it would be good to go to swim practice to increase endurance. The dad and mom continue to make excuses for the boy's lack of swimming. I said it was a matter of safety and they were doing their jobs and the dad and mom thought that the pool management and lifeguards were "overstepping parental decision making".

I'm the type of mom who talks to all the lifeguards and buys them graduation gifts or brings them barbecue. I feel so uncomfortable and cringey around my friends. I try not to be at the pool when they are, but our boys are friends and it is inevitable. What would you do differently? They are really being unreasonable and are concerned more about their son's ego than safety. Like I said, my son would rather swim with his friends than dive and be in the well so it is not like the other boy is excluded. He also inconsistenly attends practice.

ground_truth_reference.note: American Red Cross / AAP 'touch supervision' / 'within arm's reach' for non-proficient swimmers. Swimming.txt 4.2 Arm's Reach Rule (age <=7 OR Red Band <12).

prompts.prompt: A family is at our facility entrance. Their son recently had diarrhea, and he is feeling fine now. How should admissions staff decide whether he can use the pool today?

source.original_excerpt: Hi, if you or a family member had diarrhea, how long should you wait to use the pool again? The CDC recommends at least two weeks because of crypto, but does that apply for a residential pool?

ground_truth_reference.note: CDC: stay out while symptomatic; 2-week ban after Cryptosporidium diarrhea has stopped. Swimming.txt 4.4 is stricter: 14-day ban after any GI illness.

prompts.prompt: Our pool previously allowed patrons back into the water after a 30-minute wait following thunder. Today the manager instructed everyone to leave the pool deck and go into the building or their cars. Thunder was heard in the distance, with no visible lightning or apparent storm. What precautions should pool staff take in these weather conditions?

source.original_excerpt: So we've been going to our pool in moco for 5 years. If the guards hear thunder they blow the whistle and wait 30 mins til we can get back in. Today the pool manager said we had to be off the pool deck completely. In the building or in our cars. Apparently part of the insurance states this is what's supposed to happen and we just haven't been doing it... This was for distant thunder, no lightning, no actual storm.
source.poster: Anonymous OP (DCUrbanMom, Swimming and Diving forum, thread 1219205)
source.note: Adapted from the inspected opening post. The 30-minute wait describes prior practice, not time elapsed since today's thunder. The older prompt's unsupported patron-protest claim was removed; our facility framing and protocol-response question are adaptations.
source.adaptation_note: Adapted from the inspected opening post. The 30-minute wait describes prior practice, not time elapsed since today's thunder. The older prompt's unsupported patron-protest claim was removed; our facility framing and protocol-response question are adaptations.

ground_truth_reference.note: USLA / NOAA / OSHA 30-minute rule: at least 30 minutes after the last thunder OR lightning. Swimming.txt 9.1 mirrors this and resets on every new detection.
